extracted.intended_audience: NRC license applicants, parties, their counsel, and NRC adjudicatory and staff personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and disclosure rules for NRC adjudicatory proceedings, including ex parte communications, separation of functions, public inspection and withholding of documents, notice/docketing requirements, consolidation and hearings on site suitability and multi-site licensing matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt service and public record of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications received by a Commission adjudicatory employee must be promptly served on the parties and placed in the public record of the proceeding; for oral communications, a written summary must be served and placed in the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for knowing ex parte violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a communication knowingly made or knowingly caused to be made in violation of ex parte rules, the Commission or presiding adjudicatory employee may require the party to show cause why its claim or interest should not be dismissed, denied, disregarded, or otherwise adversely affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: When ex parte prohibitions apply
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibitions on ex parte communications apply when a notice of hearing or comparable order is issued in accordance with specified sections (§§ 2.104(a), 2.105(e)(2), 2.202(c), 2.205(e), or 2.312) or whenever the interested person or adjudicatory employee responsible for the communication has knowledge that such a notice will be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibitions cease to apply to communications relevant to the merits of a full or partial initial decision when the time for Commission review has expired (§ 2.341).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions to ex parte prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The ex parte prohibitions do not apply to specified categories of communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated exemptions include requests/provision of status reports; communications specifically permitted by statute or regulation; communications to/from OGC about matters pending before a court/agency; communications regarding generic issues (public health/safety, rulemakings, budgetary planning) not associated with resolution of a pending proceeding; and communications in contested proceedings and uncontested mandatory proceedings regarding an undisputed issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions general bar
rubrics_metrics.description: Any NRC officer or employee engaged in investigative or litigating functions in a proceeding (or in a factually related proceeding) may not participate in or advise a Commission adjudicatory employee about the initial or final decision on a disputed issue in that proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed exceptions are limited and specified (see separate entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted participation under separation of functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions to the separation-of-functions bar: the investigative/litigating employee may participate only as a witness or counsel; through a written communication served on all parties and made on-the-record; or through an oral communication made with reasonable prior notice to all parties and with reasonable opportunity for all parties to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to separation of functions communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications to or from any Commission adjudicatory employee are not prohibited if they concern the status of a proceeding; matters specifically permitted by statute or regulation; NRC participation in matters pending before a court or another agency; or generic issues involving public health, safety, or other statutory responsibilities not associated with resolution of a pending proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-level/specific official communications allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications to or from Commissioners, their personal staffs, Office of Commission Appellate Adjudication employees, Commission adjudicatory employees in the OGC, and the Secretary and Office of the Secretary employees are permitted regarding initiation/direction of investigations or enforcement; supervision to ensure compliance with agency policies; staff priorities/schedules or allocation of resources; and general regulatory, scientific, or engineering principles that are useful and not contested in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such communications must not be associated by the adjudicatory employee or the investigative/litigating employee with the resolution of any pending proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation and service of prohibited separation communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Commission adjudicatory employee who receives a communication prohibited by the separation-of-functions rule must ensure that it, and any responses, are placed in the public record and served on the parties; oral communications require a written summary served and placed in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/timing trigger for separation prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The separation-of-functions prohibitions apply when a notice of hearing or comparable order is issued (per listed sections) or whenever an NRC officer/employee who is or has reasonable cause to believe they will perform investigative/litigating functions, or an adjudicatory employee has knowledge that such a notice will be issued; they cease to apply to disputed issues pertinent to a full or partial initial decision when time for Commission review has expired (§ 2.341).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation does not apply to uncontested proceedings or to an undisputed issue in contested initial licensing proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No conduit via permitted adjudicatory communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications to, from, and between Commission adjudicatory employees that are not prohibited may not serve as a conduit for a communication that otherwise would be prohibited or for an ex parte communication that otherwise would be prohibited by § 2.347.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and opportunity to controvert facts/opinions from authorized communications
rubrics_metrics.description: If an initial/final decision rests in whole or in part on fact or opinion obtained as a result of a communication authorized by the separation rule, the substance of the communication must be specified in the record and every party must be afforded an opportunity to controvert it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parties had no prior opportunity to controvert before decision, they may do so by petition for review of an initial decision or petition for reconsideration of a final decision, clearly and concisely setting forth the contrary information or argument; cross-examination or rebuttal evidence may be afforded if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Final NRC records and documents (including correspondence regarding licensing, rulemaking, etc.) shall be made available for inspection and copying on the NRC website and/or at the NRC Public Document Room unless the NRC determines, after balancing the submitter's interest in nondisclosure against the public interest in disclosure, that there is a compelling reason for nondisclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This availability applies except for matters falling within specified exemption categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption: national defense/foreign policy classified information
rubrics_metrics.description: Records specifically authorized under criteria established by Executive order to be kept secret in the interest of national defense or foreign policy, and that are in fact properly classified under that Executive order, may be withheld from public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption: internal personnel rules and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Records related solely to the internal personnel rules and practices of the Commission are exempt from public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption: statutory nondisclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Information specifically exempted from disclosure by statute (other than 5 U.S.C. 552(b)) may be withheld, but only if the statute requires withholding without discretion or establishes particular criteria or types of matters to be withheld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption: trade secrets and confidential commercial/financial information
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade secrets and commercial or financial information obtained from a person that are privileged or confidential may be withheld from public disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special procedures and showing (including affidavit and marking requirements) apply when seeking withholding under this category (see related entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption: interagency/intra-agency memoranda (deliberative process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interagency or intra-agency memorandums or letters that would not be available by law to a party other than an agency in litigation with the agency may be withheld under the deliberative process privilege, except that the privilege shall not apply to records created 25 years or more before the date of request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption: personnel and medical files
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel and medical files and similar files, the disclosure of which would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy, may be withheld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption: law enforcement records (with specific subfactors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records compiled for law enforcement purposes may be withheld to the extent that production could reasonably be expected to: interfere with enforcement proceedings; deprive a person of a right to a fair trial or impartial adjudication; constitute an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy; disclose identity of a confidential source; disclose techniques/procedures or guidelines for investigations risking circumvention of law; or endanger life/physical safety of any individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption: financial institution examination reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Information contained in or related to examination, operating, or condition reports prepared by or for an agency responsible for regulation or supervision of financial institutions is exempt from disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption: geological and geophysical data concerning wells
rubrics_metrics.description: Geological and geophysical information and data, including maps, concerning wells may be withheld from public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure: marking documents when requesting withholding
rubrics_metrics.description: A submitter seeking to have a document or portion withheld must request withholding at the time the document is submitted and must mark the document so the NRC can readily identify the material sought to be withheld. The first page and each successive page containing such information must be marked with language substantially similar to: 'confidential information submitted under 10 CFR 2.390', 'withhold from public disclosure under 10 CFR 2.390', or 'proprietary.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each document/page must indicate adjacent to the information (or per paragraph if entire page) the basis (e.g., trade secret, personal privacy) for proposing withholding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit requirement for withholding requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for personal privacy information, a request for withholding must be accompanied by an affidavit which: (A) identifies the document/part sought to be withheld; (B) identifies the official position of the person making the affidavit; (C) declares the basis for proposing withholding encompassing considerations in § 2.390(a); (D) includes a specific statement of the harm that would result from disclosure; and (E) indicates the locations in the document of all information sought to be withheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may waive affidavit requirements in appropriate circumstances; personal privacy information is not subject to the affidavit requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade secret withholding affidavit special requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit supporting a withholding request based on trade secret/commercial/financial information must contain a full statement of the reason for claiming withholding and must address with specificity the considerations listed in paragraph (b)(4) (e.g., whether held in confidence, customarily held, transmitted in confidence, available in public sources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitted by a company, the affidavit must be executed by an officer or upper-level management official delegated that function and authorized to apply for withholding on behalf of the company; the information sought to be withheld should be incorporated into a separate document and appropriately marked, and is subject to §§ 9.17/9.19 of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission balancing test for withholding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will determine whether the information is a trade secret or privileged/confidential commercial or financial information and then decide whether the public's right to be apprised of the basis and effects of the proposed action outweighs the demonstrated concern for protection of competitive position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the record is deemed irrelevant or unnecessary to the Commission's functions, it may be returned to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection/ protective arrangements when withholding granted
rubrics_metrics.description: Withholding from public inspection does not affect the right, if any, of persons properly and directly concerned to inspect the document; the Commission may require inspection under a protective agreement by contractor personnel or government officials other than NRC officials, by the presiding officer in a proceeding, and under protective order by the parties to a proceeding. In camera hearings may be held when withheld information is produced or offered in evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commission later determines the information should be disclosed, the information and transcript of any in camera session will be made publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission determinations on withholding: notice and reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may grant or deny a withholding request. If granted, the Commission will notify the submitter of its determination. If denied, the Commission will provide the submitter with a statement of reasons and specify a reasonable date when the document will be available on the NRC website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document will not be returned to the submitter when denial is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of documents requested by submitter
rubrics_metrics.description: A submitter desiring to withdraw a document from Commission consideration may request return; the document will be returned unless it: (i) forms part of the basis of an official agency decision; (ii) is contained in a document made available to or prepared for an NRC advisory committee; (iii) was revealed or relied upon in an open Commission meeting; (iv) has been requested in a FOIA request; or (v) was obtained during an investigation by the NRC Office of Investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories considered commercial or financial information
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain information is specifically considered commercial/financial within § 9.17(a)(4) and subject to § 9.19: (1) correspondence and reports to/from the NRC concerning a licensee's or applicant's physical protection, classified matter protection, or material control and accounting program for special nuclear material (unless designated Safeguards Information or classified); and (2) information submitted in confidence by a foreign source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction/distribution authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting information to the NRC for consideration in licensing or regulatory activities is deemed to constitute authority for the NRC to reproduce and distribute sufficient copies to carry out the Commission's official responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer/Commission may issue consistent orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer or the Commission may, with reference to NRC records/documents made available pursuant to § 2.390, issue orders consistent with § 2.390 and § 2.705(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: multi-site identical-design licensing proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart D procedures apply to licensing proceedings considering multiple applications for licenses to construct and/or operate nuclear power reactors of identical design to be located at multiple sites (applications under appendix N of part 50 or part 52 or § 53.1470).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing for construction/combined license applications (appendix N/§53.1470)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications under appendix N or § 53.1470 for construction permits or combined licenses, the Secretary will issue notices of hearing pursuant to § 2.104; the notice will state the time and place of hearings on any separate phase of the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate hearings and consolidation on separate issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission or presiding officer may order separate hearings on particular phases of proceedings (e.g., design acceptability in context of site parameters or environmental matters). Two or more proceedings may be consolidated for hearing on that phase under § 2.317 if consolidation is conducive to proper dispatch and the ends of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In specifying place of consolidated hearing, due regard must be given to convenience and necessity of parties, petitioners, their attorneys/representatives, and the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of proposed action for operating licenses (appendix N/§53.1470)
rubrics_metrics.description: For operating license applications under appendix N or § 53.1470, if the Commission has not found a hearing to be in the public interest, the Commission or the Director, Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation, will publish a notice of proposed action in the Federal Register pursuant to § 2.105 as soon as practicable after applications are docketed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing requests and petitions for leave to intervene
rubrics_metrics.description: If a hearing request and/or petition for leave to intervene is filed within the time prescribed in the notice of proposed action and a notice of hearing or order has been issued, the Commission or presiding officer may order separate hearings on particular phases and/or consolidate proceedings as described in § 2.402.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial initial decisions in consolidated hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: At conclusion of a hearing under the subpart, the presiding officer will render a partial initial decision on the common design; such partial decisions may be appealed under § 2.341. No construction permit, full-power operating license, or combined license will be issued until an initial decision has been issued on all phases of the hearing and all issues under the Act and NEPA appropriate to the proceeding have been resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of decisions on separate issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters reserved for consideration in one phase of the hearing shall not be considered at another phase except on the basis of significant new information that substantially affects the conclusions reached at the other phase or other good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of other sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of subparts A, C, G, L, and N relating to construction permits, operating licenses, and combined licenses apply to those permits/licenses subject to this subpart, except as may be qualified by this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and notice requirements for manufacturing-license hearings (subpart E)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications under subpart F of part 52 or subpart H of part 53 for a license to manufacture reactors for unspecified sites, the Secretary will issue a notice of hearing to be published in the Federal Register at least 30 days before the date set for hearing. The notice will state time, place and nature of the hearing/prehearing conference; authority under which hearing held; matters of fact and law to be considered; and the time for filing answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice shall comply with § 2.104(f). Place of hearing will be Washington, DC, or another location the Commission deems appropriate. The 30‑day requirement does not apply to a presiding officer's published notice after the initial notice is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary/limited-scope procedures for early partial decisions on site suitability (subpart F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart F prescribes procedures for early submittal of site suitability information and hearings and early partial decisions on site suitability in connection with applications for construction permits/combined licenses for certain facilities; it also covers requests to conduct activities authorized by § 50.10(d) in advance of issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain sections of subpart F have an expiration/cessation date unless extended following public input (see § 2.600(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fees for early site-suitability review
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application requesting early review of site suitability issues must be accompanied by any fee required by § 50.30(e) and part 170 of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and docketing: initial completeness and notification timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Each part of an application submitted for early site-suitability review will be initially treated as tendered; if a part is incomplete and unacceptable for processing, the Director of the Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation will inform the applicant of deficiencies. Such determinations of completeness will generally be made within 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required for part one completeness (site selection/part one docketing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part one of an application will not be considered complete unless it contains proposed findings as required by § 2.101(a-1)(1)(i), describes the applicant's site selection process, specifies the extent the process considers alternative sites, explains relationship between that process and the early site-suitability review request, and briefly describes the applicant's long-range plans for ultimate development of the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon docketing part one, the Director will publish a Federal Register notice and send to the State Governor (or appropriate official) a notice requesting comments within 120 days (or other specified time) on initiation or outcome of an early site review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing on early site-suitability issues (modification and supplemental notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant requests an early review and hearing on site suitability, the notice of hearing will be modified to relate only to the site suitability issues under review. After docketing part two, a supplementary notice of hearing will be published for remaining unresolved issues, providing timeframes to file petitions to intervene and opportunities for state representatives and limited appearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing party obligation after supplementary notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A person permitted to intervene under the initial notice on site suitability issues who was not dismissed or did not withdraw may continue to participate in remaining unresolved issues provided they file within the time prescribed a notice of intent to continue as a party, with a supporting affidavit identifying the specific aspects they wish to continue on and setting forth with particularity the basis for their contentions regarding each aspect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A non‑timely notice may lead to dismissal absent a substantial showing of good cause with particular reference to factors in § 2.309(c)(1)(i)-(iv) and (d). The notice will be ruled upon by the Commission or presiding officer designated to rule on petitions to intervene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of Atomic Safety and Licensing Board membership
rubrics_metrics.description: To the maximum extent practicable, the membership of any Atomic Safety and Licensing Board designated to preside over remaining unresolved issues will be the same as the membership designated to preside over the initial site-suitability hearing.
